source.title: Simulation-Supervised Foundation Models for Retention Time Prediction in High-Performance Liquid Chromatography beyond Experimental Data Coverage
source.authors: Stephen Wu; Yuxuan Han; Yasuhiro Mito; Y. Watabe; Yoshihiro Hayashi; H. Takaya; Takuya Kubo; Ryo Yoshida

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests a power-law scaling relationship in a new setting: molecular simulation-to-experimental transfer for chromatographic retention-time prediction, with error measured against simulation-data size rather than language-model parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own scaling results for retention-time prediction error versus PolyOmics simulation-data size; these bear on V5. It does not test language-model pretraining loss scaling, extrapolation to larger language-model runs, compute-optimal allocation, architecture-shape effects, downstream language-model task predictability, or fit-dependence. The cited language-model scaling results are not this study's results. Other architecture and OOD benchmark results do not measure the power-law behavior named by V5.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own curve of retention-time prediction error against auxiliary simulation-data size (about three decades) for a molecular graph model. It calls this a significant power-law relationship, which bears on V5 in a transfer/auxiliary-supervision regime outside text pretraining. No language-model loss, compute allocation, shape, downstream LM tasks or fit-choice results are reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that RT-prediction error decreases systematically with simulation-data size, following a significant power law. Shuffling property values across molecules eliminates this trend, so they attribute the scaling to molecular information in the simulated properties. Separately, they find the overall simulation benefit modest in Molecule-OOD and Method-OOD but more pronounced in Joint-OOD with few-shot adaptation.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures retention-time prediction error against the amount of molecular simulation data used for auxiliary supervision, rather than language-model held-out loss against parameter count, training tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The scaling trend depends on whether simulation-property values retain their associations with molecules: it appears for the original properties and is absent after random permutation.
record.problems: The reported scaling evidence is specific to one molecular Sim2Real retention-time prediction setting. The paper reports a slope and significance tests but does not give a fitted power-law exponent in the provided text. The scaling analysis uses ten seeds.
record.rows_left_out: Other architecture comparisons, OOD adaptation results, and baseline benchmarks were not included because they do not measure the power-law scaling behavior named by V5. Cited results from prior work were also excluded.

untested.parts: Image/video models and repeated-data training. Scaling with model parameters or compute. Scaling in the Method-OOD and Joint-OOD settings (the scaling curve is reported only for Molecule-OOD). Scaling of a pretraining loss, as opposed to downstream task error. A fitted power-law exponent or extrapolation, which is not given in the main text.

missing.what: Simulation-data scaling details: per-size MAPE values and any fitted power-law exponent or functional form. Needed to confirm the power-law (versus log-linear) form.
Difference between original and shuffled slopes (paired t-test p = 0.025). Not recorded as a row.

record.verdict_notes: The scaled quantity is auxiliary simulation data (number of PolyOmics entries) used in multitask training, not model size, compute or main-task training data. The measure is downstream test MAPE, not a pretraining loss, so its bearing on V5's 'same power-law form' is indirect. The reader's limits_scope label based on the shuffled control was removed: random-label controls do not qualify the version. The scaling curve covers only the Molecule-OOD setting, where the authors themselves describe the simulation benefit as limited.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether language-model power laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation trends.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.

The study tests simulation-supervised molecular transfer for retention-time prediction only. It does not test image or video models, repeated-data training, fine-tuning or transfer settings beyond this Sim2Real application, or other modalities and training regimes.
Predictability of downstream language-model task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices, and bending of language-model scaling curves.

rows.subject: E8
rows.stage_stated: Joint RT and PolyOmics-property multitask learning
rows.operation_detail: Jointly trained with increasing amounts of PolyOmics simulation data; measured Molecule-OOD RT-prediction error
rows.measure: Improvement in MAPE per decade of PolyOmics data
rows.uncertainty: ±0.14 percentage points; one-sample t-test against zero, p = 0.004
rows.note: The paper reports that MAPE decreases systematically as simulation data increases. This is error scaling against simulation-data size, not language-model loss scaling against parameters, tokens, or compute.

rows.subject: E8
rows.stage_stated: Joint RT and PolyOmics-property multitask learning with property values randomly permuted across molecules
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the simulation-data scaling analysis after randomly permuting each property across molecules
rows.measure: Improvement in MAPE per decade of PolyOmics data
rows.uncertainty: ±0.16 percentage points; one-sample t-test against zero, p = 0.91
rows.note: The paper reports no significant scaling for the shuffled-property control; its performance is comparable to the simulation-free reference.
rows.check: Shuffled-property control: the permuted data carries no molecular information, so a flat curve does not bear on whether real-data scaling follows a power law. It validates r1's interpretation rather than qualifying V5.

rows.subject: E8
rows.stage_stated: Joint RT and PolyOmics-property multitask learning
rows.operation_detail: Compared Molecule-OOD MAPE at the full simulation-data scale with the simulation-free reference
rows.note: The paper also reports a 1.43 percentage-point paired difference between the original and shuffled-property models at full scale, p = 0.025.
rows.check: A single full-scale comparison of E8 with the simulation-free E2 (19.22% vs 20.36% MAPE). It shows a benefit of auxiliary supervision, not a scaling relationship. The MAPE figures are correct.

rows.subject: E8
rows.stage_stated: Joint RT and PolyOmics-property multitask learning with property values randomly permuted across molecules
rows.operation_detail: Compared shuffled-property model MAPE at the full simulation-data scale with the simulation-free reference
rows.note: The shuffled-property control did not significantly outperform the simulation-free reference.
rows.check: Shuffled-control full-scale comparison with E2. It is a validity control, not a scaling measurement for V5.

relationships.condition: E8 joint RT + PolyOmics multitask training, Molecule-OOD test MAPE, ~3 decades of simulation data, 10 seeds
relationships.reason: r1: MAPE falls 0.54 ± 0.14 pp per decade (p = 0.004), a systematic decrease the authors call a significant power law. The gain is small (~1–1.5 pp total), and the main text reports a per-decade slope rather than a fitted exponent.
relationships.display_finding: MAPE fell by 0.54±0.14 percentage points per data decade (p=0.004), totaling approximately 1–1.5 percentage points; the reported trend used a per-decade slope rather than a fitted power-law exponent.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: E8 with original PolyOmics property supervision in the Molecule-OOD setting
reader_labels.reason: MAPE improved significantly with increasing simulation-data size, at +0.54 ± 0.14 percentage points per decade (r1); full-scale E8 also outperformed the simulation-free reference (r3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: E8 with property values randomly permuted across molecules
reader_labels.reason: The scaling trend was absent and the full-scale control did not significantly outperform the simulation-free reference, indicating that the reported scaling depended on molecularly associated property information (r2, r4).
